prompt: A histogram has a tail on the **right** (bigger bin heights on the left). The distribution is:
hint: Skew is named for the side where the data trails off thinly, not the side where the bars are tall.

hints.text: Skew is named for the side where the data trails off thinly, not the side where the bars are tall.
This histogram has its tall bars on the left and a long, low tail stretching out to the right. Name the skew after the tail's side.
The tail is on the right, so the distribution is skewed right (choice B).

explanation: A symmetric distribution looks about the same on both sides, but here one side has a long tail, so it is skewed.
The direction of a skew is the direction in which the tail points, not where most of the data sits.
The tail extends to the right, so the distribution is skewed right, which is choice B.
